# Bidirectional Path-Space Differentiable Rendering
Also called: I.1 (unidirectional variant), I.2 (bidirectional variant), Our deriv

## Overview
Bidirectional Path-Space Differentiable Rendering computes gradients of a rendering equation with respect to scene parameters by discretizing the path space into a precomputed grid [S1, unofficial]. It extends the bidirectional structure of [Bidirectional Path Tracing](6666-bidirectional-path-tracing.md) by incorporating both light and eye subpaths, distinguishing itself from unidirectional variants through its use of dual importance/radiance maps [S1, unofficial].

## Shared principles
The method discretizes the joint probability density function $P(\mathbf{x}_B, \boldsymbol{\omega}_B)$ of the connection segment into a regular 3D grid precomputed before rendering [S1, unofficial]. Here, $\mathbf{x}_B$ and $\boldsymbol{\omega}_B$ denote the position and direction of the segment connecting the light subpath endpoint and the eye subpath endpoint [S1, unofficial]. Preprocessing generates two structures: a photon map by tracing photons carrying radiance information from the light source, and an importon map by tracing importons carrying importance information from the detector [S1, unofficial]. Within each grid cell $C_i$, the path contribution $F_B(\mathbf{x}_B, \boldsymbol{\omega}_B)$ is integrated by uniformly sampling $\mathbf{x}_B$ and $\boldsymbol{\omega}_B$ to yield a piecewise constant representation:
$$
P_i = \int_{C_i} F_B(\mathbf{x}_B, \boldsymbol{\omega}_B) \, d\boldsymbol{\omega}_B \, d\mathbf{x}_B
$$
[S1, unofficial]. Gradient computation leverages this discretized structure to approximate derivatives within the cells, handling non-differentiable path-space connections [S1, unofficial].

## Subtopics

### I.1 (unidirectional variant)
Computes gradients using only one subpath direction, reducing bidirectional complexity to a unidirectional path tracing framework [S1, unofficial]. It is chosen when computational resources for bidirectional sampling are limited or when scene geometry favors one direction of light transport [S1, unofficial]. Validation against finite-difference methods confirms accuracy for parameters such as branch rotation angles [S1, unofficial].

### I.2 (bidirectional variant)
Utilizes both the photon map and importon map to compute gradients across the complete bidirectional path [S1, unofficial]. It is selected for scenes requiring high-fidelity gradient estimation for both light and camera parameters, or involving complex multiple scattering [S1, unofficial].

## Background
The technique originates from research extending differentiable rendering to bidirectional path tracing scenarios [S1, unofficial]. It addresses the challenge of computing gradients where subpath connectivity is non-differentiable by discretizing path space with photon and importon maps, providing a robust derivative estimation method for optimization tasks in computer graphics [S1, unofficial].
